steps.name: Registration with the Portfolio Office
steps.todo: Register your service with the Portfolio Office
guidance: The Portfolio Office gives your service a reference number for every stage gate.

steps.name: Service tiering
guidance: Your service transition manager agrees a tier with you. It sets how fast live incidents are fixed.

steps.name: Solution Design Authority
guidance: The Solution Design Authority approves your architecture before you build on it.

steps.name: Technical Design Authority

timing.text: The authority needs 2 weeks' notice.
The review takes 2 weeks.
Allow 12 weeks to change the build if they ask for changes.

guidance: Explain why you need each tool outside the CDP standard stack, and who will support it.

conditions.text: Name a team to support each tool outside the standard stack

steps.notApproved: No support plan for the message queue. Add one and book the authority again.

steps.name: Service Design Review Board
guidance: The board decides whether your service can be supported when live. Your service transition manager works through your Service Design Pack with you first.

pack.name: Support model, first to third line
Service tier and hours of support
Knowledge articles for the service desk

examples: What does the board want from me?
Can I send the pack in parts?

answers.example: What does the board want from me?
paragraphs: The board wants to know your service can be supported once it is live. The guidance says your pack must cover:
bullets: who supports the service, from the service desk to your developers
its service tier and hours of support
the other systems it depends on
how you will know when it fails

paragraphs: The board's own review takes about 2 weeks. Most of the time goes on working through each section of the pack with your service transition manager.
Start the pack once your architecture is approved.

answers.example: Can I send the pack in parts?
paragraphs: Yes. Your service transition manager reviews each section as you finish it. The board only sees the whole pack.

conditions.text: Publish the knowledge articles for the service desk

steps.notApproved: No plan for backup and disaster recovery. Add one and go back to the board.

steps.name: IT health check

timing.text: Suppliers need 8 weeks' notice.
The test takes a week.
Allow 3 weeks to fix what it finds.

timingWithoutSupplier.text: The CDP security team needs 2 weeks' notice.
Allow 3 weeks to fix what it finds.

guidance: A penetration test in perf-test on CDP. Fix every critical and high finding before stage gate 4.

readiness.found: Names the supplier, the URLs and the dates.
Version 0.50.0 since 3 November 2026, in the CDP portal.

readiness.fix: Update the package first, or the testers will report it.

readiness.found: AI cannot tell if these exist. The testers will need 2.

examples: What environment does the test need?
What happens if it finds problems?

answers.example: What environment does the test need?
paragraphs: The test runs in the perf-test environment on CDP, which matches production. Deploy the version you plan to release there before the test starts.

answers.example: What happens if it finds problems?
paragraphs: You get a report that rates each finding as critical, high, medium or low. Fix every critical and high finding before stage gate 4. Agree a plan for the rest with the Defra cyber security team.

steps.notApproved: A critical finding in the sign-in flow. Fix it and book a retest.

steps.name: Platform Readiness Review

timing.text: The CDP platform team needs 6 weeks' notice.
The review takes a week.
Allow 2 weeks to fix what it finds.

guidance: The CDP platform team checks your service is ready to support. They review only services in production.

readiness.fix: Add one that says how to restart the service, read its alerts and who to call.

readiness.found: Your pipeline does not publish coverage.
readiness.fix: Send it to SonarQube Cloud from your CI pipeline.

readiness.found: They run on every pull request.
AI cannot see your alert settings. Check them in Grafana.

examples: Do I need a load test?

paragraphs: A runbook tells the support team how to keep your service running. The guidance says it must cover:
bullets: who to contact when it fails
known problems and how to fix them

answers.example: Do I need a load test?
paragraphs: Yes. Run your performance tests in the perf-test environment and keep the results. The CDP platform team asks to see them.

conditions.text: Add the service runbook to your repository

steps.notApproved: No test coverage report. Add one to your repository and book the review again.

steps.name: Accessibility audit

timing.text: Auditors need 6 weeks' notice.
The audit takes 2 weeks.
Allow 2 weeks to fix what it finds and publish your accessibility statement.

guidance: An independent auditor checks your service against WCAG 2.2 AA. Your service owner accepts the report and publishes the accessibility statement.

readiness.found: axe runs on every pull request.

readiness.text: Pages and journeys for the auditor
readiness.found: No list of what to test.
readiness.fix: Write one, with a test account for each journey. Auditors price the audit from it.

readiness.found: AI cannot test these. Try your main journey with a keyboard before you book.

examples: What do I need for stage gate 4?

answers.example: What do I need for stage gate 4?
bullets: a written audit report that confirms WCAG 2.2 AA
a plan to fix minor issues within 12 weeks of go-live

paragraphs: An independent auditor, not your own team. Ask your commercial lead which suppliers Defra already has a contract with.

conditions.text: Fix the 3 minor issues and update your accessibility statement

steps.notApproved: 2 pages cannot be used with a keyboard: upload documents and check your answers. Fix them and book a retest.

steps.name: Data protection impact assessment update
steps.todo: Start your data protection impact assessment update

timing.text: The data protection team takes about 4 weeks to review it.
Your information asset owner then signs it off, which takes about a week.

guidance: Update your alpha data protection impact assessment to match what you built. The data protection team reviews it and your information asset owner signs it off.
examples: What has to change from alpha?

answers.example: What has to change from alpha?
paragraphs: Update anything that is different from what you planned in alpha. That usually means:

steps.notApproved: The retention period is missing. Add it and send the assessment again.

steps.name: Algorithmic transparency record

timing.text: Writing and checking the record takes about 4 weeks.
Your senior responsible owner signs it off before it is published.

guidance: Explains how your service uses AI to make or support decisions. It is published on GOV.UK.
steps.notApproved: The record does not say who checks the AI's suggestions. Add it and send it again.

steps.name: Beta assessment

timing.text: The assessment team needs 6 weeks' notice.
The report comes about 2 weeks after the assessment.
Allow 2 weeks in case you need a reassessment.

guidance: A panel checks your service against the Service Standard before it opens to the public.

paragraphs: The panel spends about 4 hours with your team. You show the service and talk through how it meets each point of the Service Standard. The report comes about 2 weeks later.

conditions.text: Show research with people who use assistive technology

steps.notApproved: Not enough research with people who need help to use the service. Do more and ask for a reassessment.

steps.name: Stage gate 4
steps.statusQuestion: Where are your stage gate 4 papers up to?
steps.decidedBy: senior responsible owner, at the project board

timing.text: The Portfolio Office needs your papers 2 weeks before the board meets.

guidance: The project board reviews every decision on your route and decides whether you can go live. Send your papers once every other step is approved.

conditions.text: Confirm the service desk has the knowledge articles

steps.notApproved: The accessibility statement is not published. Publish it and come back to the next board.

steps.name: Change request

timing.text: The change advisory board needs 10 working days.

guidance: The change advisory board agrees your release date. Raise it in MyIT once stage gate 4 is approved.
examples: What goes in the change request?

answers.example: What goes in the change request?
paragraphs: The change advisory board asks for:
bullets: how you will roll back if something goes wrong
who to contact during the release

conditions.text: Share the rollback plan with the service desk

steps.notApproved: The release clashes with a change freeze. Pick another date and raise it again.
